units.title: One pipeline should replace scattered product logging
units.claim: A single pipeline should collect, enrich and land product-analytics events in the warehouse, so funnel questions (such as how many new accounts finish onboarding) no longer need hand-exported CSV files.
units.explanation: Why the proposal exists.

units.title: SDKs batch events to a collector over HTTPS
units.claim: Web and mobile SDKs batch events and send them to a collector service over HTTPS every 10 seconds, or sooner when the app goes to the background.
units.explanation: Entry point of the design.

units.title: What an event carries
units.claim: Each event carries an event name, a timestamp, an anonymous device id and, for signed-in users, an account id.
units.explanation: Detail of the payload.

omission.reason: Payload detail; not needed to understand the design or its gaps.

units.title: The collector rejects events that don't match a registered schema
units.claim: The collector validates each event against the schema registry and rejects events that do not match a registered schema.
units.explanation: The quality gate of the pipeline. What then happens to rejected events is an open question (ku.rejected-events-unknown).

units.title: Accepted events go to the analytics.events topic (kept 7 days)
units.claim: Accepted events are published to the analytics.events topic on the message bus, which keeps them for 7 days.
units.explanation: The hand-off between collection and enrichment.

units.title: Enrichment adds plan tier and region to each event
units.claim: An enrichment step consumes the topic and adds account attributes such as plan tier and region; an event whose account can't be found is passed on without them.
units.explanation: The middle of the pipeline.

units.title: How enrichment uses the user service is not stated
units.claim: Enrichment 'uses' the user service, but the source doesn't say how: a call per event, a cached lookup and a read from a replica are all consistent with the text.
units.explanation: An ambiguous relationship. It qualifies the enrichment component, so wherever enrichment is shown the uncertainty about this dependency goes with it; the edge must not be drawn as a confident 'calls' or 'reads'.

related.note: The load constraint argues against a per-event call but doesn't settle it.

review.reason: The kind of dependency is unknown; a person must confirm it with the authors.

units.title: The user service should stay lightly loaded
units.claim: The user service is expected to stay lightly loaded, so enrichment should avoid adding much traffic to it.
units.explanation: A stated constraint that bears on the ambiguous dependency.

units.title: Enriched events land in the warehouse for dashboards
units.claim: Enriched events are written to the warehouse, where the analytics team builds dashboards, starting with the onboarding funnel and weekly active accounts per plan tier.
units.explanation: The end of the pipeline. Its write cadence is disputed (ku.freshness-conflict), so the claim states no cadence.

units.title: PMs want adoption data during launches
units.claim: Product managers want to see feature adoption as it happens, especially during launches, and launch reviews usually happen within 2 hours of a release.
units.explanation: Why the freshness conflict matters.

units.title: Hourly batches or real time? The proposal says both
units.claim: The design section says enriched events are written to the warehouse in hourly batches; the freshness section says events reach the warehouse in real time. The source does not resolve which is meant.
units.explanation: A direct contradiction. Both values must be shown together and flagged; neither may be presented as the design.

review.reason: Contradictory statements; the authors must say which is intended.

units.title: Raw events: 30 days or 90 days? The proposal says both
units.claim: The retention section keeps raw events for 30 days; the components table says warehouse raw events are kept for 90 days. The source does not resolve which is meant.
units.explanation: A direct contradiction between text and table.

review.reason: Contradictory values; the authors must say which is intended.

units.title: A fixed deletion period limits access-request searches
units.claim: Deleting raw events after a fixed period also limits what an access request has to search.
units.explanation: The reason for a raw-event retention limit (whichever value is right).

omission.reason: Rationale; the conflict itself is what must be shown.

units.title: Aggregate-table retention is TBD
units.claim: How long the aggregated tables are kept is TBD; the source only says they are kept longer than raw events.
units.explanation: Missing information.

units.title: Every event type must be registered, and schemas are versioned
units.claim: Every event type must be registered before clients can send it; schemas are versioned, and a breaking change needs a new version, not an edit.
units.explanation: Stated rule of the schema registry.

units.title: Nobody owns the schema registry yet
units.claim: Ownership of the schema registry has not been decided (TBD in the table); the platform team and the data team have each suggested the other.
units.explanation: A gap with a disagreement attached. No owner may be filled in.

units.title: No emails or free text; IPs truncated at the collector
units.claim: Events must not contain email addresses or free-text input from users, and the collector truncates IP addresses before an event is published.
units.explanation: Stated privacy rules.

units.title: Not for monitoring, not a revenue record
units.claim: The pipeline is not for operational monitoring or alerting, and it will not replace the billing system's records of revenue.
units.explanation: Scope limits.

omission.reason: Scope note; useful but not part of the design or its gaps.

units.title: Platform team runs collection, data team runs enrichment and the warehouse
units.claim: The platform team owns the collector and the topic; the data team owns enrichment and the warehouse raw events.
units.explanation: Stated ownership from the components table (the registry's owner is the gap, ku.registry-owner-unknown).

omission.reason: May be left out, but must never be extended to the registry.

units.title: Phase 1: web sign-up and checkout events
units.claim: Phase 1 covers the web app's sign-up and checkout events and is expected to take about 6 weeks for 2 engineers.
units.explanation: What is planned first.

units.title: Phase 2 (mobile) has no date
units.claim: Phase 2 adds mobile events once the mobile SDK is ready; no date has been set.
units.explanation: A dependency with no date.

units.title: Running cost has not been estimated
units.claim: The cost of running the pipeline has not been estimated yet.
units.explanation: Missing information; no figure may be invented.

units.title: What happens to rejected events is open
units.claim: It is open whether events the collector rejects are dropped or kept somewhere for debugging.
units.explanation: The only statement about rejected events is a question.

units.title: Same schemas for mobile and web?
units.claim: It is open whether mobile events should use the same schemas as web events.
units.explanation: An open question from the source's own list.

units.title: Approval is asked for phase 1, with questions settled in parallel
units.claim: The proposal asks for approval to start phase 1 while the open questions are settled in parallel.
units.explanation: The decision requested of the reader.

mustNotClaim.claim: Raw events are kept for 90 days. (or: for 30 days.)
mustNotClaim.why: The source gives both values; stating one silently resolves the conflict.

mustNotClaim.claim: Events reach the warehouse in real time. (or: in hourly batches.)
mustNotClaim.why: The source says both; stating one as the design silently resolves the conflict.

mustNotClaim.claim: The platform team (or the data team) owns the schema registry.
Enrichment calls the user service synchronously for every event. (or: reads from a user-service replica.)
mustNotClaim.why: The source only says 'uses'; the kind of dependency is not stated.

mustNotClaim.claim: Rejected events are written to a dead-letter queue.
mustNotClaim.why: Invented: what happens to rejected events is an open question.

mustNotClaim.claim: Rejected events are dropped. (or: kept for debugging.)
mustNotClaim.why: The source asks exactly this (u39); stating either answer silently settles an open question.

mustNotClaim.claim: The pipeline will cost about $X per month.
